A1.justification: Both PDFs describe preference discerning, Mender, and the same five-axis benchmark. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original recommendation and steering experiments, model ablations, efficiency measurements, and preference-quality judgments in Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results and preference-quality measurements. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The LLM preference-generation pipeline, RQ-VAE semantic IDs, language encoder with a randomly initialized decoder, MenderTok/MenderEmb variants, and data-augmentation objectives are retained. Expanded explanations do not establish a changed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games, and Steam across the same five scenarios. Yelp appears in the dataset-statistics table in both versions; v2 adds no Yelp evaluation or new test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains TIGER, VocabExtRND, LC-Rec, and VocabExtLM. The traditional comparators in Table 2 and SASRec efficiency comparison in Table 7 also remain unchanged. V2's new main-text reference to Table 2 does not introduce additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix F replaces the account of 22 participants judging 20 scenarios each with manual inspection lacking an evaluator count, while retaining 440 scenarios and 2200 preferences. V2 also describes 20 recommendations per scenario, making the sampling unit less clear. This revises the reported validation protocol without establishing a rerun; the benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Preference-input, data-mixture, encoder-scaling, user-embedding, sequence-length, and preference-granularity analyses are retained. The preference-quality audit asks the same questions and displays the same outcomes; its revised protocol description adds no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across three random seeds, corresponding standard deviations in Table 6, and uncertainty values in Table 7. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and the matched result charts are unchanged. However, v2 Section 4.2 newly states that reproduced TIGER outperforms the traditional baselines. This qualitative ranking is overbroad: Table 2 retains Toys and Games Recall@10 of 0.0600 for TIGER (Ours), versus 0.0675 for SASRec and 0.0700 for S3-Rec.

T1.justification: The preference-selection definition changes its candidate set from P_u^(t) in v1 Equation 1 to P_u^(t-1) in v2 Equation 2. This corrects the admissible history to match the past-only restriction already stated in both versions' prose. The remaining mathematical content is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain intact, but the introduction narrows Mender's superiority from all evaluation axes to most axes. It also shifts emphasis from generalization to new user sequences toward dynamically adapting to changed or unseen preferences.

C2.justification: Section 5 substantially expands the limitations to cover encoder-dependent generalization, untested cold-start applicability, quadratic Transformer complexity, and the cost and quality tradeoffs of preference generation. It removes v1's incorrect statement that encoder scaling was not explored. A new Broader Impact section discusses potential echo-chamber benefits, bias amplification, and over-personalization.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a concrete code-repository link where v1's abstract promised a future release. Appendix A.2 newly specifies beam width 30; v1 only stated that the beam exceeded the retrieval-set size. This is additional implementation disclosure, not evidence of a changed decoding setting.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted references for industrial-scale semantic IDs, cold-start limitations, efficient sequence architectures, and LSTM/BERT background. It removes several earlier citations, including Hidasi et al. (2016b) and Junjie Zhang et al. (2023). The central positioning relative to TIGER and language-based recommendation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Section 3 gains background, moves Mender before benchmark construction, and separates its variants into a subsection. The limitations and Appendix F are substantially rewritten, and Broader Impact is added, producing a considerable narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: V2 adopts document-wide TMLR formatting, replacing the title panel and changing headers, typography, supplementary front matter, and float placement. It adds the five-axis overview in Figure 3, introduces labeled radar-chart subpanels, and revises several captions, including correcting Table 9's description. Existing result displays largely retain their content.

improvement.justification: The reorganized explanation, overview figure, code link, and more specific limitations improve accessibility and qualification. However, Appendix F drops the 22-participant account without explaining who produced the unchanged judgments, and Section 4.2 adds a TIGER superiority statement contradicted by Table 2. The PDFs do not resolve whether the audit revision corrects its attribution or obscures its provenance, preventing a confident net assessment of these gains and scientific-reporting concerns.
